title: PowerShell domain-user preauthentication discovery
observed_fact: Five frozen TRC-DET-003 matches were reproduced from TS-DEV-SPLUNK-PS-001. Each match is backed by a unique contributing canonical parent event ID with verified registered-artifact SHA-256, exact raw-record SHA-256, and byte locator. The complete reconstructed PowerShell ScriptBlocks contain a domain-user query together with a PreauthNotRequired selection.
inference: The reproduced behavior is consistent with domain-user preauthentication discovery activity. This is a bounded behavioral interpretation; it does not establish that any account matched the query, that credentials were obtained, or that malicious intent existed.
alternative: Authorized administration, diagnostic activity, security assessment tooling, or other legitimate PowerShell automation could issue a domain-user query using the same selection.
residual_risk: No independent same-incident corroboration is established. Query results, account matches, credential acquisition, operator intent, and any relationship to the separate Sysmon or Zeek corpora remain unestablished.
falsifier: This claim fails if the frozen TRC-DET-003 reevaluation no longer reproduces all five contributing event IDs from the registered PowerShell artifact with verified artifact and record hashes and byte locators, or if the reconstructed ScriptBlocks for those events do not contain both the domain-user query and PreauthNotRequired selection required by the frozen detector predicate.
business_impact: Observed account-discovery behavior can be relevant to identity-reconnaissance triage and may justify investigation of the originating activity. The current evidence does not establish account compromise or credential loss.
decision_required: Determine whether the observed PowerShell query was authorized and correlate it with available process, authentication, and network evidence where evidence permits. Do not initiate containment solely from this claim.

title: Sysmon Windows Firewall DomainProfile EnableFirewall zero write
observed_fact: Two frozen TRC-DET-005 matches were reproduced from TS-DEV-SPLUNK-SYSMON-001. Each match is backed by a unique contributing canonical event ID with verified registered-artifact SHA-256, exact raw-record SHA-256, and byte locator. The matched Sysmon registry_set_value semantic events record DWORD zero for the Windows Firewall DomainProfile EnableFirewall value.
inference: The reproduced events are relevant to firewall-configuration triage because they record a zero write to the DomainProfile EnableFirewall value. This does not establish final firewall state, successful disablement effect, write persistence, motive, malicious intent, or incident membership.
alternative: Authorized administration, policy application, software configuration, testing, or another legitimate configuration mechanism could produce the same registry write.
residual_risk: Effective firewall state after the writes is not observed. Write persistence, authorization, cause, motive, malicious intent, and independent same-incident corroboration remain unestablished.
falsifier: This claim fails if the frozen TRC-DET-005 reevaluation no longer reproduces both contributing event IDs from the registered Sysmon artifact with verified artifact and record hashes and byte locators, or if either semantic event no longer satisfies the frozen registry_set_value predicate targeting the Windows Firewall DomainProfile EnableFirewall value with recorded DWORD zero.
business_impact: If the recorded configuration were effective and unauthorized, firewall protection could be reduced. The current evidence supports verification and triage of firewall state and change authorization; it does not by itself establish a successful security-control disablement.
decision_required: Verify effective Windows Firewall DomainProfile state and the authorization or provenance of the two writes. Correlate with available process and security evidence where evidence permits. Containment requires additional supporting evidence.
